hook: Ion Stoica earned his PhD in computer science at Carnegie Mellon University before joining the UC Berkeley faculty in 2001, where he has remained a professor of electrical engineering and computer sciences ever since. His research group at Berkeley, first AMPLab and later RISELab, became a pipeline for widely used open source infrastructure and startups. He co-founded the video analytics company Conviva in 2006, then co-created Apache Mesos, an early cluster resource manager, before helping commercialize Apache Spark by co-founding Databricks in 2013. Working with graduate students including Robert Nishihara and Philipp Moritz, he later co-created Ray, a distributed execution framework for scaling Python and machine learning workloads, and co-founded Anyscale in 2019 to build a company around it. He continues to teach and direct systems research at Berkeley while serving in leadership roles at both companies.

quick_facts: Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences at UC Berkeley since 2001
Co-founded Databricks in 2013 to commercialize Apache Spark
Co-founded Anyscale in 2019 to commercialize the Ray distributed execution framework
Co-founded the video streaming analytics company Conviva in 2006
Co-created Apache Mesos, an early cluster resource manager, at Berkeley's AMPLab
Holds a PhD in computer science from Carnegie Mellon University

achievements.title: Co-founder of Databricks
achievements.impact: Helped commercialize Apache Spark into a data and AI platform used by a large share of the Fortune 500.

achievements.title: Co-founder of Anyscale
achievements.impact: Built a company to deliver production infrastructure around Ray, which became widely used for scaling machine learning and later large language model workloads.

achievements.title: Co-creator of Apache Mesos
achievements.impact: Contributed an early cluster resource manager that influenced later container orchestration systems.

achievements.title: Director of research labs feeding open source infrastructure
achievements.impact: Led the Berkeley AMPLab and RISELab groups whose projects, including Spark, Mesos and Ray, became foundational pieces of modern data and AI infrastructure.
